title: Where selection is rigid, and the criterion over Z_(p^k)
claim: Where selection is rigid, and the criterion over Z_(p^k). A system of knots on a k-regular k-uniform substrate (one knot per line, a linear equation with unit coefficients) fails globally when removing any one line makes it solvable; it is rigid when, after removing any line, every circuit of its solutions is a tie (two variables). (1) Over a field every global failure has corank 1, so removing a line leaves one degree of freedom and only ties: rigid, at every arity. (2) Over Z_(p^k) a system fails globally exactly when the class of its right-hand side in the cokernel is a nonzero element of every cyclic subgroup generated by the class of a line's unit vector; after removing line L the solutions are a coset of a group of order |cokernel| x |annihilator of the class of L|, and when that group is cyclic only ties remain. (3) Blurring keeps rigidity; the only proper subgroup of S3^3 and of D_p^3 (p odd) with full 2-projections is the sign-parity subgroup, so the knots of these cycle-composing groups are blurred parity, whose failures are rigid (never global on cubic substrates); a simple non-affine Mal'tsev algebra on three values has no knot on full ranges. Checked on random systems over GF(3), GF(5), GF(7) at arities 3 and 4, the Z_(p^k) criterion against brute force (Z4, Z8, Z9), cyclic kernels on random global failures over Z4, Z8, Z9, Z25, Z27, all subgroups of S3^3 generated by two elements, and 200 simple three-element algebras.
failure_conditions: A global failure of a knot system over a field with corank above 1, or with a knot after removing a line.
A system over Z_(p^k) whose global failure disagrees with the cokernel criterion.
A global failure over Z_(p^k) with a cyclic solution group after removing a line and a circuit of three or more.
A proper subgroup of S3^3 with full 2-projections other than the sign-parity subgroup.
foundation_claim_scope: Rigidity of global failures for knot laws over fields, blurred laws, S3 and D_p, and the Z_(p^k) criterion.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-01.
validation.status: checked: random global failures over three prime fields at arities 3 and 4; the criterion by brute force; cyclic kernels; subgroups of S3^3; a sample of simple three-element Mal'tsev algebras; no human or external review
validation.novelty: Linear algebra over fields and local rings is classical; the rigidity statements and the cokernel criterion for global failure are new here.
